decisions.rationale: In the title, 'phenylketonuria' is used attributively to modify the noun 'mutation' ('phenylketonuria mutation'), so it is annotated as a Modifier rather than a standalone disease mention.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: 'classic phenylketonuria' names one specific form of phenylketonuria (classic PKU) that is not further subdivided, so it is a Specific Disease; 'classic' is kept because it denotes a particular form of the disease.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §1 (Specific Disease) and §5 (Minimum necessary span; cf. Example 15)

decisions.rationale: 'PKU' is the abbreviation defined in '(PKU)' after 'classic phenylketonuria'. Abbreviation definitions are split into two separate mentions, so the short form is annotated as its own Specific Disease mention.
In 'a classic PKU phenotype', 'classic PKU' modifies the noun 'phenotype' and is not a standalone disease reference, analogous to 'colorectal cancer families' being annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: 'PKU' in 'Japanese PKU alleles' functions as a noun modifier of 'alleles' rather than naming a disease in its own right, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)

decisions.rationale: In 'the PKU mutation', 'PKU' modifies the noun 'mutation' and is used attributively, so it is annotated as a Modifier.
decisions.guideline_section: What to Annotate §3 (Disease mentions used as Modifiers)
